LD 262, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Taste Testing of Wine and Malt Liquorto Facilitate Marketing by Wholesalers (EMERGENCY)

Good morning, Sen. Hic|<man, Rep. Supica and members of the VLA committee. I am Cheryl Timberlake, a resident of Mt. Vernon. Here this morning in my capacity as the Executive Vice
President of the Maine Beverage Distributors Association.
The Maine Beverage Distributors Association (MBDA) is a group of Maine family-owned independent
distributors who provide beer, wine, and non-alcoholic beverages to retailers from every region of the state with integrity, responsibility, and high quality. For more than 75 years, MBDA has served an important role in Maine's alcohol regulatory system. MBDA distributor members serve as the
crucial industry link between beer, wine, and non-alcoholic manufacturers/suppliers and more than 4,500 Maine grocery stores, convenience stores, restaurants, bars, and other retail locations
licensed to sell alcohol to Maine consumers. MBDA services the entire state, spanning from the
northernmost regions to the southernmost tip of Maine.
MBDA wishes to thank the sponsors of LD 262, MBDA are strong supporters ofthis measure and
asked for the bill to be introduced.
As Rep. Crockett stated, the bill offers a change to existing law to accommodate a distributor taste
testing event at an unlicensed venue. MRSA 28A 1402 is attached to my testimony.
The distributor taste testing event is allowed at the wholesale licensee premise, or they may rent an
area/room from an on-premises retail license for the purpose of inviting their retail partners to attend a wine and malt liquor products taste testing.
The bill proposes to amend these provisions and adds "other unlicensed venues" as an option for
these distributor events.
For those new to taste testing's - there are several types permitted in statute: consumer tastings
and licensee tastings. LD 262 tastings are specific to licensees; distributor hosted and retailer invitees only. These events are not for the public. No consumers will be allowed.
The criteria for these events are defined in existing law in subsection 3 of the attachment:
- Distributor provides the products for the event (taxes paid) - Event conducted in a special designated area - Event is open only to invited retail licensees - After the event, the distributor shall remove all products from the retail premises
- Wine and malt liquor products may not be served to a minor or a visibly intoxicated person

In closing, I want to add emphasis to the importance of the EMERGENCY preamble. We are hopefulthe bill will be passed sooner rather than later. The ninety-clay effective date for the
bill passage will be too late for 2025 hospitality season. This will allow the State's restaurants, bars, grocery stores, beverage retailers and local craft
manufacturers to showcase their products this spring in advance of the busy summer season and allow distributors to hold taste testing events at a greater number of locations. I appreciate your time and consideration of these comments. The MBDA hopes you will support the
bill. i am happy to answer any questions and will be here at the work session.
Thank you.

262.

and consideration.

Testimony of Rep. Ed Crockett introducing
LD 262, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Taste Testing of Wine and Malt
Liquor to Facilitate Marketing by Wholesalers Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and distinguished members of the Veterans and Legal
Affairs Committee, I am Representative Ed Crockett, House District #112, which includes part of
Portland and part of Falmouth. I am sponsoring LD 262 on behalf of the Maine Beverage
Distributors Association (MBDA).
I understand that this bill might be one of the first public hearings on alcohol for the committee
this session. As a legislator in the beverage business, I am happy to introduce this bill and the
importance of taste testings.
As the summary states, this bill modifies the law governing taste-testing events held by malt liquor and wine wholesale licensees. Under current law, wholesale licensees may rent or lease an
area from a retail licensee for the purpose of inviting retail licensees to taste test wine or malt
liquor products.
The bill broadens a wholesale licensee's ability to hold such a taste-testing event by also allowing the wholesale licensee to rent or lease an unlicensed venue for that purpose.
BABLO has included this proposed change in their Department bill, LD 494 under Section A-19 on page 5. The purpose of having this stand-alone bill is to ensure the EMERGENCY preamble
is recognized so that the industry may implement the venue options for the upcoming 2025 Spring Trade shows and conduct taste testings with retail licensees at locations which may not
have a liquor license.
Outside of the legislature, I am the President of Capt'n Eli's Soda, a premium Maine soft drink
company. In this capacity, I can validate first-hand the value of distributor tastings. Product innovation is ever changing. Consumer tastes are diversified. Retailers need the taste testings to

These events are between retail licensees, both on-premises (restaurants, taverns and pubs) and off-premises accounts (grocery and convenience stores) and the distributors. There is no public involvement -- no consumers are allowed to participate in these licensees - only events.

Testimony of the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs
In Support of LD 262 An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Taste Testing of Wine and Malt Liquor to Facilitate
Marketing by Wholesalers
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans
and Legal Affairs: I am Louis Luchini and I'm the Director of the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations. I'm here to testify in support of LD 262, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the
Taste Testing of Wine and Malt Liquor to Facilitate Marketing by Wholesalers.
For background, 28 MRS �l402 allows wholesalers to conduct taste testing events on their premises or a
licensed retail premises with permission from the Bureau. These events are open only to invited retail
licensees or their authorized guests ~ not members of the general public.
This bill would allow wholesalers to host these taste testing events on unlicensed premises. The Bureau supports this legislation, and after discussions with the wholesalers, included the same provision in the
BABLO department bill, LD 494. We believe this provision will expand opportunities for both the
wholesaler and retailer communities.
Thank you for your time, and I'm happy to answer any questions.
